newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks sour on Wall St, direction unclear.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks sour on Wall St, direction unclear.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed lower on Friday, drawn down by Wall Street losses, but were seen drifting in rudderless trade in the short-term, dealers said.

End investors dominated the market with block trades seen as mainly technical and the relatively few exchange trades were concentrated on banks, where dealers said there was room to enter Spain's growing economy.
The general index fell 6.27 points, 1.04 percent, to 596.13 and the Ibex-35 lost 81.05 points, 1.18 percent, to 6,783.06.
Santander was one of few gainers, rising 25 pesetas to 4,425, in what dealers said was part of the general bank trend.
"The ugly international tone dominated trade. The short term tendency is an unknown and the only clear trend in the elevated volatility," one dealer said.
Dealers said the unusual trade would continue through the summer holiday month of August.
The banking sector, which absorbed most of the block trades, was heavily traded with Popular, Santander, BBV, Argentaria and BCH among the top 10 trade volumes of the session.
Telefonica fell 40 pesetas to 4,150 amid news of talks on a new foreign entrant in its Via Digital television platform.
